risks.note: MD&A states commodity prices (namely Solid Carbide, Steel and other related commodities) increased abnormally in very high proportion during the year. The Solid Carbide Tools business faced margin pressure as a result, and the Company's response was limited to 'trying to pass on as much cost increase as possible' to customers - i.e. pass-through is attempted, not assured. Operating profit margin fell to 16.39% from 18%.
risks.risk: Raw material price escalation in solid carbide and steel

risks.note: MD&A explicitly names 'our dependency on Automotive sector' and flags that the industry's EV initiatives and move to different fuel options will change consumer demand, requiring the Company to realign to retain a meaningful share. This is an end-market concentration risk against a structurally shifting customer base.
risks.risk: Dependence on the Automotive sector and its EV/fuel transition

risks.note: Tariffs imposed by the USA and Mexico on India led to a drop in sales; the MD&A separately notes US tariffs of initially 25% and later another 25% additional. Management describes the overall export market as 'not very encouraging' and says competition plus government protectionist policies make inroads into such markets difficult, constraining the international leg of the growth strategy.
risks.risk: Export exposure to tariffs and protectionism

risks.note: MD&A cites the continuing Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Palestine conflicts and the Iran-USA-Israel conflict as building pressure on supply chains, and warns of a world that is 'less coordinated, more risk averse and more exposed to non-linear outcomes with narrower margin of safety', where global political shocks may manifest with a lag. It also warns that if the AI investment boom factored into global growth projections is not achieved it could trigger an asset-value correction with potential for broader financial contagion. Such factors 'may have an impact on demand patterns and could potentially constrain revenue growth opportunities'.
risks.risk: Geopolitical and global macro instability affecting demand and supply chains

risks.note: The MD&A's human resources section states attrition remained a concern with substantial attrition in the lower executive cadre at a rate close to 25%, with measures only now being put in place to control it - a retention and execution risk for a precision-manufacturing business dependent on trained operators, and one the Company has quantified against itself.
risks.risk: Employee attrition, concentrated in the lower executive cadre

risks.note: The Company is subject to laws on product safety, product claims, trademarks, copyright, patents, competition, employee health and safety, environment, water and air pollution, corporate governance, listing and disclosure, employment and taxes. MD&A states that frequent changes in the legal and regulatory regime and newer regulations with multiple authorities regulating the same areas lead to complexity in compliance. The cost of such change is already visible: on the Government's notification of the Labour Codes the Company recognised an estimated impact of Rs 590 Lakhs on employee benefit obligations, and says further impact may be accounted for as rules are implemented.
risks.risk: Legal and regulatory complexity across many overlapping regimes

risks.note: MD&A states operations are increasingly dependent on IT systems and information management, that increasing digital interaction with customers, suppliers and consumers raises the need for secure and reliable infrastructure, and that the cyber-attack threat of unauthorised access, misuse of sensitive information or disruption to operations continues to increase. Exposure is rising further with the SAP S/4HANA and HRMS rollouts.

MD&A identifies power consumed for manufacturing and air cooling as a critical resource requiring active optimisation. Rooftop solar, the Company's mitigation, has 'met only partial demand', leaving the cost base exposed to grid power prices.
risks.risk: Energy cost and power availability as a critical manufacturing input

risks.note: The MD&A's human resources section states attrition remained a concern with substantial attrition in the lower executive cadre at a rate close to 25%, with measures only now being put in place to control it - a retention and execution risk for a precision-manufacturing business dependent on trained operators, and one the Company has quantified against itself.

risks.risk: Legal and regulatory complexity across many overlapping regimes
risks.note: The Company is subject to laws on product safety, product claims, trademarks, copyright, patents, competition, employee health and safety, environment, water and air pollution, corporate governance, listing and disclosure, employment and taxes. MD&A states that frequent changes in the legal and regulatory regime and newer regulations with multiple authorities regulating the same areas lead to complexity in compliance. The cost of such change is already visible: on the Government's notification of the Labour Codes the Company recognised an estimated impact of Rs 590 Lakhs on employee benefit obligations, and says further impact may be accounted for as rules are implemented.

MD&A states operations are increasingly dependent on IT systems and information management, that increasing digital interaction with customers, suppliers and consumers raises the need for secure and reliable infrastructure, and that the cyber-attack threat of unauthorised access, misuse of sensitive information or disruption to operations continues to increase. Exposure is rising further with the SAP S/4HANA and HRMS rollouts.

risks.risk: Energy cost and power availability as a critical manufacturing input
risks.note: MD&A identifies power consumed for manufacturing and air cooling as a critical resource requiring active optimisation. Rooftop solar, the Company's mitigation, has 'met only partial demand', leaving the cost base exposed to grid power prices.

business_model.title: Business (RHP)
business_model.body: The Company manufactures carbide and high-speed steel (HSS) round-cutting tools under the brand 'TOTEM', offering complete tooling solutions in internal and external threading, drilling, milling, deburring and reaming. Tools are made at a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, India, and are designed with material-specific geometries to optimise tool performance for the end-user. The Company states it is also the largest manufacturer of spring lock washers in India, serving major auto and transmission segments.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- MD&A states commodity prices (namely Solid Carbide, Steel and other related commodities) increased abnormally in very high proportion during the year. The Solid Carbide Tools business faced margin pressure as a result, and the Company's response was limited to 'trying to pass on as much cost increase as possible' to customers - i.e. pass-through is attempted, not assured. Operating profit margin fell to 16.39% from 18%.
- MD&A explicitly names 'our dependency on Automotive sector' and flags that the industry's EV initiatives and move to different fuel options will change consumer demand, requiring the Company to realign to retain a meaningful share. This is an end-market concentration risk against a structurally shifting customer base.
- Tariffs imposed by the USA and Mexico on India led to a drop in sales; the MD&A separately notes US tariffs of initially 25% and later another 25% additional. Management describes the overall export market as 'not very encouraging' and says competition plus government protectionist policies make inroads into such markets difficult, constraining the international leg of the growth strategy.
- MD&A cites the continuing Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Palestine conflicts and the Iran-USA-Israel conflict as building pressure on supply chains, and warns of a world that is 'less coordinated, more risk averse and more exposed to non-linear outcomes with narrower margin of safety', where global political shocks may manifest with a lag. It also warns that if the AI investment boom factored into global growth projections is not achieved it could trigger an asset-value correction with potential for broader financial contagion. Such factors 'may have an impact on demand patterns and could potentially constrain revenue growth opportunities'.
